```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 7, fig.height = 5)
```

Decision-analytic models in CEA must be verified and validated before their
results inform policy. Errors in transition probabilities, discounting,
dominance classification, or PSA distributions can silently produce wrong
conclusions. ShinyCEA provides a suite of automated checks that cover the
full model lifecycle, following the AdViSHE framework (Vemer et al., 2016)
and ISPOR-SMDM good modeling practices (Eddy et al., 2012).

This vignette demonstrates every validation function and how to generate
a comprehensive quality report.

## Validation Suite Overview

| Function | What it checks | When to run |
|:---------|:--------------|:-----------|
| `check_transition_matrix()` | Trace: rows sum to 1, non-negative, death monotone | After first simulate() |
| `check_probabilities_sum()` | Prob params in [0,1], groups sum to <=1 | After defining parameters |
| `check_discounting()` | Undiscounted >= discounted, rate in range | After model construction |
| `check_psa_inputs()` | Distribution-domain consistency, bounds present | Before running PSA |
| `check_dominance_logic()` | Dominated correctly identified, ICERs monotone | After deterministic run |
| `validate_model_outputs()` | Costs/QALYs non-negative, survival valid | After first run |
| `generate_validation_report()` | All of the above + score | Before publication |

## Setup

```{r load}
library(ShinyCEA)
m <- cea_sick_sicker()
params <- m$default_params()
```

## 1. Transition Matrix Checks

For Markov cohort models, the trace matrix must satisfy fundamental
properties. Every row represents a cycle's state distribution and must
sum to 1. No entry can be negative. The death state must be monotone
non-decreasing (people don't come back from death).

```{r trace-check}
pars <- stats::setNames(as.list(params$base), params$name)
res <- m$simulate(pars, "std")

checks <- check_transition_matrix(res$trace)
checks[, c("check", "status", "details")]
```

For partitioned survival models (no trace returned), the function reports
the absence rather than failing:

```{r trace-ps}
m_ps <- cea_partitioned_survival()
pars_ps <- stats::setNames(as.list(m_ps$default_params()$base),
                            m_ps$default_params()$name)
res_ps <- m_ps$simulate(pars_ps, "std")
check_transition_matrix(res_ps$trace)[, c("check", "status")]
```

## 2. Probability Checks

Probabilities must be in [0, 1], and groups of mutually exclusive
transition probabilities from the same state must sum to at most 1.

```{r prob-check}
checks <- check_probabilities_sum(params)
checks[, c("check", "status", "details")]
```

You can specify custom groups when auto-detection doesn't capture
your model's state-transition structure:

```{r prob-groups}
custom_groups <- list(
  "from_H" = c("p_HS_std", "p_HD_std"),
  "from_S1" = c("p_S1S2_std", "p_S1D_std")
)
checks <- check_probabilities_sum(params, prob_groups = custom_groups)
checks[checks$check != "Probability params found", c("check", "status", "details")]
```

### Common errors caught

- A probability of 1.5 (data entry error)
- Three transitions from one state summing to 1.2 (missing complement)
- A negative probability (sign error in a formula)

## 3. Discounting Checks

Discounting should reduce future costs and QALYs. The check compares
outputs with and without discounting and verifies that discount rate
parameters exist and are in a reasonable range.

```{r discount-check}
checks <- check_discounting(m, params)
checks[, c("check", "status", "details")]
```

### What this catches

- Discounting applied in the wrong direction (discounted > undiscounted)
- Discount rate set to an implausible value (e.g., 30%)
- Missing discount rate parameter (model always uses 0%)

## 4. PSA Input Validation

Before running a 10,000-iteration PSA, verify that every PSA-eligible
parameter has an appropriate distribution, domain-consistent bounds,
and reasonable uncertainty width.

```{r psa-check}
checks <- check_psa_inputs(params)
checks[, c("check", "status", "details")]
```

### Common errors caught

- Beta distribution with mean outside (0, 1)
- Gamma distribution with negative mean
- `include_psa = TRUE` but `distribution = "fixed"`
- Bounds spanning 10x the mean (excessively wide uncertainty)
- No bounds or SE provided (can't derive distribution shape)

## 5. Dominance Logic

After running the deterministic analysis, verify that the frontier
analysis correctly classifies strategies as dominated, extendedly
dominated, or on the frontier.

```{r dominance-check}
det <- run_deterministic(m, params, wtp = 100000)
checks <- check_dominance_logic(det)
checks[, c("check", "status", "details")]
```

### What this catches

- A strategy classified as "Dominated" that isn't actually dominated
  by any frontier strategy
- Sequential ICERs along the frontier that are not monotonically
  increasing (indicates an extended dominance error)
- Reference strategy that doesn't have the maximum NMB

## 6. Model Output Validation

Runs all strategies at base case and checks that costs, QALYs, trace,
and survival outputs are plausible and internally consistent.

```{r output-check}
checks <- validate_model_outputs(m, params)
checks[, c("check", "status", "details")]
```

### What this catches

- Negative costs or QALYs
- QALYs exceeding the time horizon (e.g., 15 QALYs in a 10-year model)
- Costs exceeding $5M per patient (flags for review, not necessarily wrong)
- Survival not starting at 1.0
- Survival outside [0, 1]
- OS < PFS at any time point
- Trace rows not summing to 1

## 7. Comprehensive Validation Report

`generate_validation_report()` runs ALL checks and compiles them into a
single report with a quality score.

```{r full-report}
report <- generate_validation_report(m)

cat("Model:", report$model_name, "\n")
cat("Score:", report$score, "/ 100\n\n")
print(report$summary)
```

### Scoring

| Finding | Penalty |
|:--------|:-------|
| Each FAIL | -5 points |
| Each WARN | -1 point |
| PASS | No penalty |
| Starting score | 100 |

A score of **80+** indicates a model ready for analysis. Below 80,
address the FAILs before proceeding.

### Detailed results

```{r report-details}
# Show non-PASS findings
issues <- report$details[report$details$status != "PASS", ]
if (nrow(issues) > 0) {
  issues[, c("category", "check", "status", "details")]
} else {
  cat("No issues found.\n")
}
```

### Export to Markdown

```{r export, eval = FALSE}
generate_validation_report(m, output_file = "validation_report.md")
```

This produces a formatted markdown file with sections for each check
category, suitable for inclusion in an HTA submission appendix or
internal quality documentation.

## Validation Workflow

The recommended workflow for model QA:

```
1. Define parameters
   └─→ validate_param_table() + check_probabilities_sum() + check_psa_inputs()

2. Build model
   └─→ validate_cea_model() (automatic in new_cea_model())

3. First simulation
   └─→ validate_model_outputs() + check_transition_matrix()

4. Deterministic analysis
   └─→ check_dominance_logic() + check_discounting()

5. Before PSA
   └─→ check_psa_inputs() (re-run after parameter edits)

6. Before publication
   └─→ generate_validation_report() → score >= 80
```

## Integration with HTA Submissions

The validation report maps to standard HTA requirements:

| ShinyCEA check | AdViSHE domain | ISPOR-SMDM TF |
|:--------------|:---------------|:---------------|
| `check_transition_matrix()` | Internal validity | Siebert et al. 2012 |
| `check_probabilities_sum()` | Internal validity | Karnon et al. 2012 |
| `check_discounting()` | Internal validity | Weinstein et al. 2003 |
| `check_psa_inputs()` | Uncertainty analysis | Briggs et al. 2012 |
| `check_dominance_logic()` | Internal validity | Caro et al. 2012 |
| `validate_model_outputs()` | Face validity | Eddy et al. 2012 |
| `generate_validation_report()` | Cross-validation | Vemer et al. 2016 |
